RGB MoCap

 

A native Windows app that turns video into editable human animation. Review and
export motion with AI processing running locally.

 Install and run

The steps below cover Windows. For the experimental x86-64 Linux AppImage and
source installation, see the Linux guide.
The AppImage was tested on WSL 2. Native Linux Mint testing is welcome.

 [!IMPORTANT]
 On Windows 11, Smart App Control in On mode may block the unsigned private
 Python runtime used by RGB MoCap. This can stop installation or launch.
 See Smart App Control troubleshooting.

1. Install Git for Windows. Use a short, writable
 installation path such as C:\RGBMoCap . Open Command Prompt to clone
 the repository. Adjust the path if you need a different folder.

 Keep the console open while the app runs. Prepare the AI model files separately

If setup fails with WinError 3 or WinError 206 and the error shows a long
path, see Windows path length troubleshooting.

To update, close the app and run update.cmd from the same folder. See the
installation guide for disk space, prerequisites
and recovery.

Updates reuse recently verified, unchanged runtimes. If PEAR or camera-alignment
support preparation fails after the base installation succeeds, the base app
remains usable; rerun install.cmd to retry the unavailable support. See
verification and repair.

 Optional model runtimes

 install.cmd prepares ExMR, FlowHMR, GVHMR and the small shared-runtime support
for PEAR live preview. Install the following only if
you use them, after the base installation:

 Model Separate setup command Installation and usage 
 --- --- --- 
 MAMMA Setup MAMMA.cmd MAMMA guide 
 PromptHMR Setup PromptHMR.cmd PromptHMR guide 
 GEM-X Setup GEMX.cmd GEM-X guide 

MAMMA and PromptHMR require Visual Studio 2022 C++ Build Tools , the Windows SDK and
 CUDA Toolkit 12.8 for local native builds. Close the app and review the
provider terms before setup. Then reopen it and prepare the selected model's
files in Model Manager . Their optional runtimes do not require each other;
 install.cmd and update.cmd do not install them.

GEM-X uses the existing ExMR Python base with its own pinned inference packages.
Run its separate setup after install.cmd , then prepare its public files in
 Model Manager . It does not require the C++ build tools or CUDA Toolkit.

PEAR reuses the base shared runtime with a small support overlay prepared by
 install.cmd and update.cmd . No separate setup or compiler is required.
Model files are prepared separately.

For optional text-prompt and click-guided Find person tracking on Windows,
run Setup SAM31.cmd after the base setup. Then choose SAM 3.1 next to
 Find person and use Auto Download on its 1.75 GB checkpoint row in
 Model Manager . SAM 3.1 uses more VRAM than Default tracking.
 Resource Mode Automatic can offload tracking state and masks to system
RAM when VRAM is tight and retry once after CUDA runs out of memory.
See the SAM 3.1 tracker guide.

 Track Face adds CPU face tracking for saved video. The 3D viewport shows
facial landmarks on SMPL-X, SMPL-H and SOMA surfaces. Export Face saves
ARKit-style coefficients alongside the chosen motion as TXT or Unreal Live Link Face CSV.
Face preview landmarks and Unreal-streamed expression coefficients use One Euro smoothing automatically. Set Neutral beside Track Face calibrates the selected person from the current frame, with saved per-person baselines and Reset. Saved face coefficients can also accompany Unreal Live Link body streaming; enable Face in the separately installed RGB MoCap Connect plugin. See Face capture and face streaming.

Install with an AI agent

After cloning, open this repository folder in a local coding agent such as Codex. The agent guide covers setup, models, capture, retargeting, projects and resources. For example, ask:

Help me install and run RGB MoCap on this Windows PC.
Read AGENTS.md and docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md first. Check the GPU and free disk space,
run install.cmd, and launch RGBMoCap.cmd. Help me prepare the ExMR model files.
Preserve existing models, projects and settings, and keep the pinned runtimes.
Tell me when I need to sign in, accept provider terms or download a file manually.

For multi-camera capture, add:

Also enable MAMMA. Follow docs/MAMMA_AGENT_SETUP.md to check the C++/CUDA tools,
run Setup_MAMMA.cmd after the required license review, and verify the native CUDA
modules. Help me prepare its models without changing the other model runtimes.

For PromptHMR instead, add:

Also enable PromptHMR. Follow docs/models/PROMPTHMR.md and docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md.
Check the C++/CUDA tools, run Setup_PromptHMR.cmd after the required license
review, verify its CUDA checks, and help prepare the exact Model Manager files.
Keep other runtimes and existing projects unchanged.

MAMMA's agent setup guide and the PromptHMR guide include build checks and recovery. Provider login and license acceptance remain your responsibility; do not put passwords or account tokens in the agent chat.

features.title: Features
features.html:
• Optionally use RIFE frame interpolation for videos below 30 fps before offline reconstruction. The standard converter is the default. RIFE setup and usage

  • Manage model files across workflows in one window. See which workflows share each file, filter to dedicated models, and remove installed files after reviewing the affected workflows. Model Manager guide

  • Reconstruct one or several people and preview the body mesh and animation bones.

  • Reduce sliding with foot/palm contact correction and editable contact timings.

  • Retarget motion to Mixamo FBX, VRM and PMX humanoid characters.

  • Export source animation as FBX or BVH (Generic/Blender or 3ds Max Biped), with FBX A/T reference poses, an optional leading reference frame, per-person origin placement and symmetrical rest pose; export characters as FBX with or without meshes, or PMX character motion as VMD for MMD.

  • Export portable Blender projects with source animation, video and saved cameras; MAMMA can include animated body meshes and every camera.

  • Export animation for the stock UE5 Manny or Quinn skeleton. Include the bundled skinned mesh when the Unreal project has no mannequin assets. UE5 mannequin FBX guide

  • Export the current take, all takes for checked people, or individual takes. The export dialog shows what to do for each unavailable take. Export guide

  • Stream selected people's bones to Blender during playback or scrubbing, then bake their full recorded motion into Blender Actions. Download the Blender add-on ZIP · Installation and controls

  • Stream motion to UE5 Manny and Quinn or to MetaHuman actors through Unreal Live Link. MetaHumans also support tracked expressions. Prebuilt Windows bundles and installation · Controls and manual retargeting

  • Preview and correct GEM-X's native SOMA motion, retarget to humanoid characters, and export the Native77 skeleton as FBX or BVH. The Blender bundle includes the evaluated surface and input video.

  • Save side-by-side input video and the current 3D viewport as MP4 with File > Export Preview... (offline models).

  • Inspect source-video/bone alignment in Camera Preview and display saved cameras in 3D, with optional background rotation refinement for FlowHMR/ExMR.

  • Save projects with separate results for each AI model.

  • Reduce FlowHMR memory use with query-batched attention and optional sparse hand sampling; optional HaMeR refines fingers. See controls and trade-offs and measured time/memory comparisons.

  • Reduce camera-estimation VRAM with default-on VGGT-Ω OPT in FlowHMR and automatic MAMMA calibration. It also works in Low Memory mode. Measured camera VRAM

  • Track webcam or video input in real time with PEAR's experimental body/finger bone preview; tracking and poses may be unstable.
